entries.definition: good-natured tolerance of delay or incompetence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal, and it makes the same tolerance sound deliberately held back - a reaction withheld where *patience* is simply an even temper.

entries.definition: a disposition to kindness and compassion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest of the three and the widest: not endurance of an annoyance but a whole bent toward kindness and compassion.
examples: the victor's grace in treating the vanquished

entries.definition: good-natured tolerance of delay or incompetence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain praise for a temper that absorbs delay or bungling without souring, the trait named as if it cost nothing.
examples: I recollected my dear Elizabeth and Jane, and for their sakes had patience with her.
She tried, however, to compose herself to answer him with patience

entries.definition: harshness of manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and it locates the fault in bearing and manner rather than in feeling, which makes the condemnation cool and considered.

entries.definition: a dislike of anything that causes delay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The narrowest fault here - it fastens on one trigger, delay, and so criticises without alleging the loss of control that *temper* does.
examples: His impatience showed in every queue he ever stood in.

entries.definition: harshness of manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for the same harsh manner, felt as a cutting edge on how someone deals with you rather than *asperity*'s formal verdict on them.

entries.definition: a disposition to exhibit uncontrolled anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest charge in the family: not a passing mood but a settled liability to anger that gets out of hand, so attributing it is an accusation about character.
examples: his temper was well known to all his employees
He has a temper, and everyone at work knows to keep out of his way.

entries.definition: secrecy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Informal and clipped where *secrecy* is abstract, shrinking the same trait to one syllable of keeping quiet.
examples: mum's the word

entries.definition: the trait of keeping things secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat name for the trait, taking no view on whether what is kept back ought to be.
examples: Having said thus much, I feel no doubt of your secrecy.
There were few people on whose secrecy she would have more confidently depended

entries.definition: the trait of keeping things secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the trait by its outward result — nothing said — where *secrecy* names the keeping back itself.

entries.definition: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Leans on the not-caring half of the sense rather than the calm half, so the composure reads as something missing and carries a faint reproach that *unconcern* escapes.
examples: He listened to her with perfect indifference
With an air of indifference, he soon afterwards added

entries.definition: the trait of remaining calm and seeming not to care; a casual lack of concern
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Weights the calm, casual side instead — an untroubled evenness that may be only a seeming, and names the absent worry without *indifference*'s hint that nothing is felt at all.

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A respectable-looking surface lent to something so it seems defensible; it does not hide the thing underneath, it only shades it.
examples: the situation soon took on a different color

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling of the same deceptive surface: a creditable tint lent to something so it passes, and no more than a tint, where *disguise* covers.
examples: His story was only a colour to hide what he had really done.

entries.definition: an outward semblance that misrepresents the true nature of something
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most covering word here, not a shading of the truth but an outward form that actively misrepresents what lies under it.
examples: the theatrical notion of disguise is always associated with catastrophe in his stories

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the idea of a polish worked onto the outside, so the deceit is one of finish rather than of concealment as in *disguise*.
examples: he tried to give his falsehood the gloss of moral sanction

entries.definition: an artful or simulated semblance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same artful or simulated semblance as *pretence*, but framed as a form put on and worn, so the deceit sits in the assuming of it.
examples: under the guise of friendship he betrayed them

entries.definition: an artful or simulated semblance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling, and it foregrounds the artfulness, naming the semblance as something got up rather than something merely appearing.

entries.definition: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The barest word in the set, naming only the outward or token form and leaving the misleading to be inferred, where *pretence* puts the artifice on show.
examples: he hoped his claims would have a semblance of authenticity

entries.definition: a blemish on the skin that is formed before birth
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Traces the blemish to birth rather than to any injury, so nothing is blamed for it.

entries.definition: a mark or flaw that spoils the appearance of something (especially on a person's body)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps the damage at the level of appearance — the thing is spoiled to look at, where *defect* calls it faulty.
examples: a facial blemish

entries.definition: a place or area that has been burned (especially on a person's body)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the place by the violence that made it, which gives it a weight *mark* has not.

entries.definition: a mark left after a small piece has been chopped or broken off of something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The colourless name for the same loss *chip* reports, with none of the sound of breaking in it.

entries.definition: a mark left after a small piece has been chopped or broken off of something
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Something is gone rather than merely marked, and the word makes the loss sound abrupt.

entries.definition: a blemish resulting from a break without complete separation of the parts
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Graver than *chip* or *scratch*, since the break runs through the thing and only the parts still holding together keep it whole.
examples: there was a crack in the mirror

entries.definition: a mark or flaw that spoils the appearance of something (especially on a person's body)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the spoiling mark as a fault, so the thing carrying it is judged wanting rather than merely marked.
examples: A faint scar was the only defect on her smooth skin.

entries.definition: an impression in a surface (as made by a blow)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The surface has given way under a blow without breaking, so nothing is lost and it stays milder than *chip*.

entries.definition: an impression in a surface (as made by a blow)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and belittling — the same blow-struck impression as *dent*, named in a way that makes light of it.
